title: How BeyondTheBlack 2026 Shapes the Future of Corporate Finance
summary: Explore how the BeyondTheBlack 2026 global event series from BlackLine unifies corporate finance leaders to explore governed AI and autonomous financial operations.
body_text: Key Takeaways • A Shared Global Vision : BeyondTheBlack 2026 brings together corporate leaders across London, Paris, & Orlando to establish a strategic blueprint for Agentic Financial Operations. • Unifying Your Systems : Implementing successful finance automation requires an ERP-agnostic control plane like BlackLine Studio360 to bridge the gap between legacy systems. • Auditable Intelligence : Every AI innovation showcased at the event utilizes a "glass box" design that keeps human control and auditability at the center of financial operations. Leading the Charge Toward Future-Ready Financial Operations The rapid evolution of corporate accounting requires enterprise leaders to unite human expertise with secure, governed technology. The global BeyondTheBlack 2026 event series from BlackLine delivers the ultimate strategic roadmap, showcasing how a unified data plane and collaborative digital workers empower modern organizations to achieve highly auditable, automated financial operations. Regulatory demands are intensifying, and finance executives must evolve their processes to maintain a competitive edge. This event series provides the critical knowledge and peer connections necessary to guide your organization through this transition with confidence. What’s New at BeyondTheBlack 2026? The 2026 global tour introduces major advancements designed to help organizations transition to autonomous financial operations. Here is what is new at the conference this year: • The BlackLine Studio360 Platform : Discover how this ERP-agnostic control plane unifies data across disparate systems, including SAP, Oracle, Workday, and Snowflake. • Live Agentic Financial Operations Demonstrations : See how autonomous AI agents work alongside human professionals to automate complex, multi-step accounting workflows. • Expanded Regional Forums : With specialized events in London, Paris, and Orlando, the tour offers content addressing local compliance requirements and market dynamics. • Interactive Auditor Workshops : Learn from the leading accounting firms about how to design and maintain fully compliant, audit-ready automated processes. Major Topics to Elevate Your F&A Performance The agenda for BeyondTheBlack 2026 is structured to address the most pressing challenges facing the Office of the CFO. Through curated sessions and panels, attendees will gain actionable insights to improve operational efficiency and strengthen financial controls. Key agenda highlights include: • Deploying Governed AI Responsibly: Learn to implement AI solutions that maintain a transparent, "glass box" architecture to support strict auditing standards. • Mastering Intercompany Accounting: Discover strategies to resolve transfer pricing, tax compliance, and multi-currency complexities across global legal entities. • Optimizing the Financial Close: Explore methods to transition from manual, reactive month-end processes to a continuous close. • Accelerating Invoice-to-Cash Workflows: Understand how advanced automation reduces days sales outstanding and optimizes working capital management. • Navigating Regulatory Reforms: Gain practical guidance on adapting to regulatory changes, including UK Corporate Reform and other global compliance frameworks. Why Executive Presence at BeyondTheBlack 2026 Is Essential Today, finance and accounting departments are facing unprecedented pressures. Organizations need to navigate fluctuating economic landscapes, manage growing transaction data volumes, and comply with strict regulatory frameworks. For executive leaders, attending BeyondTheBlack represents a vital opportunity to align your corporate roadmap with the cutting-edge innovations redefining the industry. CFOs, controllers, and vice presidents of finance must move beyond traditional oversight and actively lead digital transformation. Engaging with industry peers at this global forum provides a unique environment to share strategies and establish a scalable framework for future-ready financial operations. How the Conference Addresses the Office of the CFO Corporate accounting is shifting from manual, reactive tasks toward real-time, strategic oversight. To facilitate this transition, the conference offers customized tracks that help executives deploy AI solutions from BlackLine responsibly. "BeyondTheBlack is about giving finance and accounting leaders practical, real-world insight into how they can modernize with confidence," said Owen Ryan, Chief Executive Officer of BlackLine, in an announcement shared on Business Wire . This real-world focus helps executive leaders design an efficient, resilient F&A function, transforming finance departments into strategic centers of enterprise value. How BeyondTheBlack London Set the Stage for AI Trust & Governance The 2026 global tour commenced with BeyondTheBlack London on Tuesday, April 14, 2026, at the London Hilton. The London forum gathered top finance minds to discuss AI trust, data control, and local regulatory changes, including UK Corporate Reform. Philippe Omer-Decugis, General Manager of EMEA at BlackLine, noted that the event was "a valuable opportunity for finance professionals to learn directly from their peers, partners and BlackLine leaders." The discussions around UK Corporate Reform and EMEA compliance emphasized that modern financial transformation must be built on a foundation of absolute trust, transparent data controls, and robust governance models. Why Verity AI Serves as the Catalyst for Autonomous Accounting Once a unified data foundation is established, organizations can leverage the cognitive power of Verity™ , BlackLine’s purpose-built AI for finance. Verity introduces a coordinated digital workforce of specialized agents. Together, they automate core processes like intercompany accounting and invoice-to-cash workflows with total precision. According to market data , enterprise-level software commands 75% of the market value, illustrating the massive demand for secure, governed AI solutions capable of scaling across complex business environments. By integrating these tools, finance teams can shift from transactional processing to knowledge-based analysis. How to Make the Most of BeyondTheBlack To maximize the value of your attendance, it is essential to approach the event with a clear, strategic plan. Preparing in advance ensures you capture the insights most relevant to your organization. Consider these strategies to optimize your experience: • Select Your Tracks in Advance: Align your daily agenda with your primary business goals, whether you are focused on financial close, controls, or intercompany accounting. • Engage with Product Experts: Schedule dedicated consultation sessions with technical specialists from BlackLine to discuss your specific ERP landscape. • Participate in Hands-on Labs: Visit the interactive product sandbox to experience new tools like BlackLine Studio360 and Verity AI in a guided environment. • Network with Peers: Attend regional receptions and roundtable discussions to connect with other financial leaders, sharing best practices and solving operational challenges. While You Are in Orlando While the core of BeyondTheBlack is focused on financial innovation, the flagship North American conference also offers attendees an opportunity to connect and unwind in vibrant Orlando. Taking time to recharge and network outside the session rooms is an important part of the global event experience. Where to Eat Orlando features a celebrated culinary scene that extends far beyond theme park dining. Attendees can explore world-class fine dining, including MICHELIN-starred and recognized restaurants in stylish areas like Winter Park and Lake Nona. The dining districts near the Orange County Convention Center offer exceptional venues for team dinners, networking events, or client entertainment. What to Do Known as the theme park capital of the world, Orlando delivers unparalleled entertainment. Attendees can experience iconic attractions at Walt Disney World and Universal Orlando Resort, explore the lively entertainment venues on International Drive, or play a round of golf on championship courses under the Florida sun. Join Us at BeyondTheBlack 2026 The future of corporate finance is being shaped by leaders who are willing to embrace governed automation, secure AI, and unified data architectures. BeyondTheBlack 2026 is the premier platform to gain the strategic insight and practical tools required to lead this transformation. Register for the priority list to secure your pass for the BeyondTheBlack 2026 global flagship conference. Frequently Asked Questions About BeyondTheBlack Who Should Attend the BeyondTheBlack Conferences? BeyondTheBlack is designed for CFOs, controllers, CAOs, accounting managers, and F&A specialists who want to automate manual workflows, build audit-ready processes, and explore modern financial technology. What Are the Main Product Solutions Showcased at the Events? The conferences highlight the comprehensive portfolio from BlackLine, including solutions for the Financial Close, Intercompany, Invoice-to-Cash, and Consolidation & Financial Analytics. Attendees will also receive deep-dive training on the newly introduced BlackLine Studio360 platform and the advanced capabilities of the Verity AI platform. How Do These Events Address AI Compliance & Auditing Standards? All featured technologies utilize a "glass box" architecture, ensuring that every automated action has a clear, auditable trail. Dedicated workshops also provide practical strategies for collaborating with external auditors to ensure compliance with global standards, including UK Corporate Reform and SOX regulations. title: Swapping stories malfunctions on Android
summary: Hi C/c from Adding tags and swapping stories malfunctions on Android (…) when swapping stories if I’m swapping forward, then one story back and then forward, the first story forward is ok, the second one is empty but stories after are ok. If I’m swapping forward, then one story back and then continue to swap back, all stories after the first one are empty. <give us some feedback!> app version: 14.5.4 (279) android version: 17 (CP2A.260705.006) device: Google Pixel 7a (lynx) username: G...
body_text: Guybrush July 17, 2026, 8:46am 1 Hi C/c from Adding tags and swapping stories malfunctions on Android (…) when swapping stories if I’m swapping forward, then one story back and then forward, the first story forward is ok, the second one is empty but stories after are ok. If I’m swapping forward, then one story back and then continue to swap back, all stories after the first one are empty. <give us some feedback!> app version: 14.5.4 (279) android version: 17 (CP2A.260705.006) device: Google Pixel 7a (lynx) username: Guybrush server: default pending actions: pre:0 post:0 premium: yes prefetch: no notifications: no keep read: no thumbs: yes Guybrush July 24, 2026, 12:52pm 2 Up samuelclay July 24, 2026, 3:41pm 3 Thanks for bumping this. I reproduced the July 17 report using NewsBlur 14.5.4 (279). The regression came from a recent WebView memory optimization. A story’s WebView could be recreated while the app still considered its content loaded, leaving it blank after swiping back and forth. The fix now detects empty recreated WebViews and reloads their story content. The fix was committed today and will ship in the next Android release after 14.5.4. The exact version number and Play Store date have not been set yet but should be out soon. Guybrush July 28, 2026, 6:31pm 4 It seems to work now with the last update, thanks

title: Mirion Supports Advanced Reactor Criticality Milestones Through U.S. DOE Reactor Pilot Program
summary: Mirion Technologies and Paragon Energy Solutions Provide Radiation Monitoring and Nuclear Safety Systems for Advanced Reactor Demonstrations …...
body_text: Mirion Supports Advanced Reactor Criticality Milestones Through U.S. DOE Reactor Pilot Program July 10, 2026 8:15 am EDT Download as PDF Mirion Technologies and Paragon Energy Solutions Provide Radiation Monitoring and Nuclear Safety Systems for Advanced Reactor Demonstrations ATLANTA--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Mirion , a global leader in radiation safety, science, and medicine, announced today that its Mirion Technologies and Paragon Energy Solutions businesses supported multiple advanced reactor designs that have achieved criticality milestones in the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Reactor Pilot Program, established under Executive Order 14301. In May 2025, the Administration issued executive orders to strengthen and accelerate the U.S. nuclear industry. Executive Order 14301 directed the DOE to bring at least three advanced reactor designs to criticality by July 4, 2026. Of the 11 projects initially selected, four achieved criticality — the ability to sustain a controlled nuclear chain reaction. Across these efforts, Mirion Technologies and Paragon provided products, systems, and expertise spanning reactor protection, neutron flux monitoring, radiation monitoring, health physics, radiation protection and radiochemistry. These capabilities helped developers reach criticality safely and advance their projects. Congratulating the DOE, Idaho National Laboratory and Reactor Developers Mirion congratulates the U.S. DOE, Idaho National Laboratory (INL) and the reactor developers on these landmark achievements. As host to a number of participating reactor efforts and a national leader in advancing reactor innovation, INL provided the infrastructure, expertise, and testing capability that helped make these milestones possible. The program’s success reflects the shared commitment of the DOE, its national laboratories, and industry partners to demonstrating that the United States can develop and deploy advanced nuclear technology at pace. “Achieving criticality is a defining milestone in advanced reactor development, and we are proud to support the teams building the next generation of nuclear energy,” said Tighe Smith, Chief Nuclear Officer of Mirion and Paragon. “What this program has shown is that an ambitious schedule is achievable when government, the national laboratories and industry work as one team toward a shared goal. That momentum is a real breakthrough. It proves we can move quickly and, importantly, safely sustain that pace as advanced nuclear moves from demonstration toward broad deployment.” Mirion Nuclear Solutions — Mirion Technologies, Paragon Energy Solutions and Certrec — provides integrated capabilities spanning reactor safety, radiation monitoring, regulatory compliance and operational readiness from demonstration to commercial deployment. About Mirion Mirion is a global leader in radiation safety, science and medicine, empowering innovations that deliver vital protection while harnessing the transformative potential of ionizing radiation across a diversity of end markets. Focused on nuclear and safety, the Mirion Technologies group is committed to powering advancements in nuclear energy through proven radiation safety technologies and expertise. Dedicated to driving better patient outcomes, the Mirion Medical group is focused on improving quality in cancer care through its broad range of solutions that enhance the delivery and ensure safety across the medical landscape. Headquartered in Atlanta (GA – USA), Mirion employs approximately 3,200 people and operates in 12 countries. Learn more at mirion.com . title: How I Scaled an App from $0 to $200K ARR in 6 Months with Apple Search Ads
summary: Apple Search Ads are a powerful marketing tool, here's 8 tips to get the most out of them.
body_text: Apple Search Ads (ASA) can transform subscription app growth, but getting started can be daunting. Do you use basic ads (spoiler: no ), advanced ads, how much do you use for bids? The questions can pile up. I spent $100,000 on ASA campaigns, and using it as my primary marketing lever, I was able to scale an app from $0 to $200,000 ARR in six months. Today, I'll share the actionable steps that anyone can use to kickstart growth through ASA. I've broken them out into eight, digestible steps to follow. 1. Set up attribution first Before running any ASA campaign, ensure you're sending ASA attribution data to tools like Superwall , Mixpanel, or AppsFlyer. This is critical, and you can't miss this step. Why? This data allows you to do two essential things: Understand which keywords drive high-converting installs. And, you can track ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) to optimize campaigns. Without proper attribution, you're flying blind and will almost certainly run the risk of blowing money. ASA campaigns rarely "just work" out of the box. It takes experimentation, tweaking and iteration. You won't know how to do any of that properly without attribution. 2. Avoid keywords with "free" This step is easy: Steer clear of bidding on keywords that include "free." While they may generate taps, these users rarely convert to paying subscribers. In the end, you're likely looking at low conversion rates paired with wasted spend. This also ties into step one. We need to know what works so we can avoid situations exactly like this one. 3. Choose targeted keywords Obviously, some keywords are naturally going to perform better than others. Instead of using broad terms like "pilates," focus on long-tail keywords that fit your app's target market. Going back to "pilates", something like "wall pilates workout" will typically yield better results. Even better? These keywords are generally less competitive, and they often attract users with higher intent to subscribe. This makes sense, because you're casting a narrow net on purpose to find the right people for the problems that your app solves. 4. Double down on high-LTV keywords This next step ties directly into step one and your attribution pipeline. Here, we need to analyze attribution data to identify: Keywords with the highest subscription conversion rates. And, keywords that generate the most revenue. Group these keywords by theme, and then turn around and create Custom Product Pages (CPPs) tailored to each one. This approach all but guarantees to: Increase your conversion rates. Lower your cost per install (CPI). And, accelerate campaign performance. A custom product page example in App Store Connect At this point, you've created an extremely capable marketing flywheel where you know which ASA keywords are working and leading to paying customers. But now? You've made the messaging even better than it was before using CPPs. 5. Leverage competitor keywords as a benchmark Competitor keywords are crucial. As Zach Yadegari pointed out in a recent podcast, high-performing ASA campaigns on competitor keywords indicate that your product is on par with or better than theirs. So, what about poor performance? Put simply, this is data which typically indicates that their product simply is solving the particular problem domain better than you are. It's an important signal that you need to pay attention to with humility and action. Don't get discouraged, just iterate and improve. 6. Optimize your app's conversion rates Even the best ASA campaigns won't work if your product has poor conversion rates. You can be good at ASA campaigns and bad at converting users. To have a well-performing app, you need both. To that end, focus on improving: Onboarding: Ensure users understand your app's value proposition quickly. Do they get to that "Aha!" moment quick enough? Do they start to feel why not using your app going forward would be a little more painful? Install-to-Trial Conversion Rate: Fine-tune your paywalls and pricing, and realize that this is a process that will never stop. Superwall is the best tool out there for that job. 7. Leverage second-time offers One of the most impactful changes you can make is to implement second-time offers. After onboarding, show a discounted paywall to users who dismiss the initial paywall. Don't confuse this with a transaction abandoned paywall, here — users didn't attempt to purchase anything. An example of what a second-time offer could look like In that case, offering a discount can capture revenue that you may have never had in the first place. This approach can significantly boost your conversion rate and ROAS (which is critical for healthy, long-term ASA campaigns). If you want to be more targeted and not offer this to everyone, use AppsFlyer media source parameters along with Superwall's campaign filters to trigger second-time offers only for users who installed the app via ASA. Campaign filter to target users via AppsFlyer media sources 8. Send personalized follow-ups Send ASA attribution data to CRM tools like Iterable or OneSignal. Then, use this data to: Trigger push notifications or pop-ups offering discounts or trials. Run personalized campaigns to re-engage users who installed via ASA. These follow-ups should help you improve retention and drive that last extra bit of revenue. Wrapping up ASA can deliver phenomenal results, but they need to be executed correctly. From choosing the right keywords, to implementing second-time offers, or using custom product pages — these strategies can help you maximize the ROI of your ad spend to help scale your app's revenue quickly.

title: Verizon One Talk alternatives: 7 We actually tested
summary: Looking for Verizon One Talk alternatives? We compare 7 Verizon One Talk competitors like Quo, along with pricing and top features.
body_text: For current Verizon customers, Verizon One Talk may seem like a solid business phone solution. All phone numbers come with basic features you can bundle with your existing plan. However, the One Talk app is far from a perfect phone service — and for thousands of small businesses, the features aren’t a good value for the price. Between contractual obligations and inconsistent service, most people end up looking elsewhere. In this guide, we’ll share seven Verizon One Talk alternatives that might be what you’re looking for. But first, let’s look at everything you need to know about Verizon One Talk. How we tested Verizon One Talk alternatives We measured Verizon One Talk’s competitors based on seven factors: Call quality and reliability. We tested and reviewed user reports on uptime and audio clarity. We also looked at how each provider performed for teams splitting calls across mobile and desk phones, since that’s core to what One Talk offers. Setup and onboarding. We assessed how easy it was to create an account, port an existing number, and get a team calling within a day. We ruled out options with slow onboarding or tools you couldn’t set up without speaking to a customer support or sales rep. Overall value. We compared pricing tiers, per-number costs, and add-on fees. We looked for tools that offered the most value at an affordable price. Third-party integrations. We checked which providers connect with tools teams already use. This included CRMs, help desks, and field service management software. Design and ease of use. We evaluated how quickly a non-technical person could set up features like call routing without needing a rep on the phone. Customer support. We looked at what support channels each provider offers. We also checked how fast they responded and whether users report getting stuck without help — a recurring complaint with One Talk. Reviews from real users. We analyzed customer feedback across review platforms. Then, we synthesized it to find common strengths, recurring issues, and overall satisfaction. 7 Verizon One Talk alternatives Verizon One Talk may not be everything you thought it was. Fortunately, seven business phone service solutions may be a better option for your company. Provider Best for Starting price Unlimited calling to US & Canada Unlimited SMS/MMS to US & Canada Additional phone numbers Verizon One Talk Verizon users $20 per line Depends on Verizon plan Depends on Verizon plan $15 per number per month Quo Small and growing businesses $15 per user per month ✓ ✓ $5 per number per month Grasshopper Phone extensions $14 per user per month ✓ ✓ $9 per number per month RingCentral Deskphone rentals $20 per user per month ✓, limited toll-free minutes X, 25 messages per user per month $4.99 per number per month CloudTalk Power dialers $25 per user per month US and Canadian customers only Requires upgrade $9 per number per month Aircall Call centers $30 per user per month, three-user minimum ✓ X $6 per number per month Dialpad Advanced AI needs $15 per user per month ✓ X Requires upgrade, then $5 to $15 per month Nextiva Omnichannel communication $15 per user per month X X Undisclosed fee 1. Quo: Best Verizon One Talk alternative for growing teams Pros Unlimited calls and texts in the US and Canada Local, toll-free, and vanity numbers are available Shared numbers to split responsibility for incoming calls and texts Texting automations On-demand and automatic call recording and transcription Integrations with 9,000+ third-party apps, including HubSpot and Salesforce AI features for call transcriptions, summaries, and action items Virtual receptionist to cover calls 24/7 HIPAA compliance with a signed BAA Cons No verification through two-factor authentication* *Nearly all virtual phone numbers share this problem. For safety reasons, companies like Facebook, Uber, and Google rarely let you authenticate accounts through a virtual phone number. Quo is a modern business phone system you can use on your computer, smartphone, or tablet. Each user gets a local or toll-free US or Canadian business phone number with unlimited calling and texting. This way, you can stay accessible and build better relationships without worrying about costs adding up. All Quo numbers come with their own inbox. This keeps a record of all the phone activity on that number. You can easily see business call recordings , voice messages, and texts in a single view under individual contact threads. Want your team to split responsibility for incoming calls? With shared numbers , everyone can call and text from the same number. Here’s what a shared inbox looks like on Quo: Unlike Verizon One Talk, Quo doesn’t require you to be a tech genius to set up your call flow. Want calls to go to an emergency number after hours? Need calls to ring your team in a specific order during hours? What if you want to add a phone menu? Use Quo’s drag-and-drop call flow builder to set up your routing in a way that fits you . Don’t try to make your business fit your phone. For additional coverage, Quo offers a 24/7 AI voice agent , Sona . Once trained on your business, Sona can answer calls when your team is unavailable, qualify leads, take messages, and handle routine questions. You can customize its responses and test it with demo calls before going live so it fits your workflow from day one. Switching from Verizon One Talk because of its call unreliability? Quo has a high uptime history . But if you do ever struggle on a call, you can open Quo’s call quality metrics right in the middle of it and see exactly what’s going wrong. Instead of guessing why the connection is bad or letting the customer sit through it, you can spot the issue and fix it in real time. Unlike One Talk, you can get started in just minutes using Quo, and if you have any questions, our support team is ready to answer. When you sign up for Quo , you get clear pricing upfront. Plans start at just $15 per user per month. We make it easy to choose a plan that meets your needs right now , which makes it easier to upgrade whenever the time is right — no preloaded devices or long contracts are required. Key features of Quo Free calls and texts, both SMS and MMS, to Canada and the US Phone menus or auto attendants Voicemail transcriptions that can be accessed from any device Automatic call recording for all phone numbers Integrations with dozens of apps, including Claude and CRMs like HubSpot , Salesforce , Jobber , Zoho CRM , and Pipedrive 9,000+ third-party integrations via Zapier and Make AI conversation analytics built in and also through connection to tools like Claude Auto-reply text options and saved text templates with snippets AI-generated message responses Call summaries and transcripts Mobile, desktop, and web apps across Mac, Windows, iPhone, Android, and a browser AI contact suggestions Quo pricing Quo offers transparent pricing and some of the best rates in the industry for must-have business phone features: Starter: $15 per user per month for shared phone numbers, voicemail transcriptions , free calls and texts in the US and Canada, and dozens of ways to streamline your business’s phone communication Business: $23 per user per month for IVR auto-attendant , call transferring, CRM integrations, analytics, and more advanced features Scale: $35 per user per month for AI call tags, inbound phone support, dedicated onboarding, and priority chat and email support How to switch and port your number from Verizon One Talk Get a virtual phone number in minutes Try for free Looking to move your existing phone number to Quo? Porting your number is free, easy, and a great way to keep using an existing number that customers already recognize. Set up a Quo account if you don’t already have one. Complete our two-minute porting form by logging into the Quo web or desktop app. Hang tight; the porting process to get a number from your existing carrier to our platform can take up to 10 business days. 2. Grasshopper: Best for phone extensions Pros Affordable pricing Unlimited users, with an upgrade Unlimited extensions, with upgrades Cons No integrations besides Google Voice Some standard features like call recording and simultaneous call handling require an upgrade Major texting limitations Grasshopper is a fairly basic Verizon One Talk alternative. It has the baseline features you might need, like calling and texting, call forwarding, and voicemail transcription. The base plan is suited for one user and gives you one phone number and a single extension. If you’re not a solopreneur, you can upgrade for more users and extensions. But there are some limitations to know: There’s no way to purchase additional extensions without upgrading. Even then, you’ll have to pay $3 per extension and $9 per number. That’s nearly double the cost of some VoIP solutions. You can’t send international text messages. Keep in mind, with Grasshopper, US states Hawaii and Alaska count as international locations. You can’t send MMS through Grasshopper toll-free numbers . You can’t send group texts unless you’re using a local phone number. This is why hundreds of former customers have switched to Grasshopper competitors . Key features of Grasshopper Virtual fax Phone extensions MP3 voicemail transcriptions for email Call forwarding Reporting Grasshopper pricing Grasshopper’s pricing plans depend on how many phone numbers and extensions you need: True Solo: $14 per month for one user, one phone number, and one extension Solo Plus: $25 per month for unlimited users, one phone number, three extensions, call recording, IVR, and simultaneous ring Small Business: $55 per month for unlimited users, four phone numbers, and unlimited extensions 3. RingCentral: Best for deskphone rentals Pros Built-in video conferencing Unlimited calls in the US and Canada Cons Limited texts Limited toll-free minutes Limited storage space If you’re still using deskphones but aren’t happy with the Verizon ones, you might consider RingCentral . This Verizon One Talk alternative offers desk phone rentals with their multi-year contracts. You can buy or rent them for as low as $4 per month, along with paying for a subscription to use RingCentral. But you should be aware of some limitations with RingCentral’s features: Toll-free minutes are limited. For example, you only get 100 toll-free minutes on the base plan. That’s not even two hours of calling per month. Text messages are limited to 25 SMS per user per month. One conversation with slightly more back-and-forth, and you’re paying additional fees. You don’t get unlimited storage for your performance reports or call recordings on any plan. For example, your call history is deleted after 9–12 months. Reviews for their customer support are also pretty mixed. While some report efficient service, many users across platforms like Reddit and G2 have complaints. Here’s how one user puts it: “[I dislike the] customer service. I have opened 3 cases about the same issue in [the] past 8-9 days. I get canned responses, and nobody knows what they are talking about.” — G2 Key features of RingCentral Video meetings Team messaging File sharing Visual voicemail IVR RingCentral pricing RingCentral’s pricing offers four plans, which depend on how many users you have. For one to five users, the pricing is: Core: $20 per user per month for 100 toll-free minutes, 25 texts per user, and basic call recording Advanced: $25 per user per month for 1,000 toll-free minutes, 100 texts per user, advanced call recording, and advanced call queues Ultra: $35 per user per month for 10,000 toll-free minutes, 200 texts per user, more storage, and device analytics and alerts Customer Engagement Bundle: Custom pricing for shared SMS inbox, company reply templates, SMS compliance management, call back from queue, wait time and place alerts, and all AI virtual Assistant features 4. CloudTalk: Best Verizon One Talk alternative with a power dialer Pros Numbers in 160+ countries Unlimited inbound and intracompany calls Call queues and queue callbacks Cons Outbound calls cost extra International texts require an upgrade SMS requires an upgrade Integrations require an upgrade CloudTalk is a solid Verizon One Talk competitor for mid-sized and large sales and customer support teams. It gives you a second phone number in over 160 countries, and the app is available in eight languages. Plus, features like call queues and preferred agent routing help support teams stay organized at scale. With an add-on or multiple upgrades, you can get CloudTalk’s power dialer feature. This lets reps automatically dial the next number on their list as soon as a call ends, so they get through their list more quickly. But a bit of bad news if you’re a business that relies on cold calls or dialing out to your customers. Outbound calls are priced per minute, which quickly adds to your bill. You also have to pay extra for SMS and MMS messaging, which is only available on the second most expensive plan. Even caller ID requires an upgrade, which is something most phone services offer for free. Planning to leave Verizon One Talk because of its high costs? Unless you really need some of CloudTalk’s unique features, it’s probably not the alternative for you. Key features of CloudTalk Unlimited inbound calls International number support Unlimited callers in queues Parallel calling Click-to-call options International phone numbers Desktop, iOS, and Android apps CloudTalk pricing CloudTalk’s plans give you three tiers to choose from: Starter: $25 per user per month for unlimited inbound calling in the US and Canada, international numbers, call recording, ring groups, call queuing, and click-to-call from CRM Essential: $29 per user per month for SMS and MMS, business hours and time-based routing, IVR, and skill and condition-based routing Expert: $49 per user per month with a three-user minimum, power dialing, call monitoring , and Salesforce integration 5. Aircall: Best for call centers Pros Unlimited inbound calls and texts in the US and Canada International numbers are available in over 100 countries Advanced call listening features Cons Three-user minimum on the base plan Outbound texts are not unlimited AI-generated call summaries require an expensive add-on Unlimited call recording storage requires an upgrade Aircall is a good Verizon One Talk alternative for larger teams that need call listening features. For example, with an upgrade, you get manager call coaching and call whispering. There’s also an AI Assist add-on that gives you talk-to-listen ratios, sentiment scoring, and call summaries. Speaking of add-ons, you can also set up WhatsApp and Salesforce Voice integrations. This makes Aircall work inside these platforms to give you the most flexibility and convenience for your customers and your team. Just know that Aircall’s pricing can be prohibitive. There’s a three-user minimum for most plans, which means the cheapest you’ll pay is $90 per month — even if you’re a solopreneur. To add to your bill, outbound texts aren’t unlimited. Aircall only includes 250 outbound SMS and 50 outbound MMS per user per month before messaging rates apply. To compare, Quo has no user minimums and gives you unlimited texting and calling in the US and Canada. You also get features like AI call summaries at a much more reasonable price point. According to one G2 reviewer : “ The biggest issue is misleading pricing and features. The basic plan does not include the power dialer, and to access it, you’re forced into a 3-seat minimum plan that costs almost $250 per month after taxes. Customer support is very difficult to reach, refund requests are refused, and billing practices feel unfair — including charges after cancellation and unexplained add-ons. ” Aircall key features 250+ integrations and API access Softphone for desktop, Android, and iOS Simultaneous calling Smart routing, with an upgrade Queue callback, with an upgrade Aircall pricing You can choose from three Aircall pricing plans: Essentials: $30 per license for unlimited inbound calls within the US and Canada, IVR, call recording, click-to-dial, SMS and MMS, with a three-license minimum Professional: $50 per license for the Salesforce integration, mandatory call tagging, and advanced analytics and call monitoring, with a three-license minimum Custom: Custom price for unlimited calls worldwide, custom analytics, and custom onboarding, with a 25-license minimum 6. Dialpad: Best for advanced AI needs Pros AI tools on every plan Video meetings on every plan Unlimited calling in the US and Canada Cons Purchasing multiple numbers requires an upgrade Zapier integration requires an upgrade Higher-tier plans have user minimums Dialpad is a Verizon One Talk competitor for large sales and support teams. Beyond standard VoIP calling, it has AI features like real-time transcription. Depending on your plan, you can also get live sentiment analysis, call scoring, AI call summaries, and more. If you’re running a high-volume sales or support team, the AI features can meaningfully reduce post-call admin work. And the analytics give managers real visibility into what’s happening on calls. But Dialpad gets expensive and restrictive fast, which is where other Verizon One Talk alternatives pull ahead. Each user gets one number, while purchasing multiple numbers requires an upgrade. Extra local numbers start at $5 per month, with more for toll-free or international numbers. And you only get integrations with Google Workspace on the base plan. Even a simple Zapier integration requires an upgrade. Speaking of upgrades, be prepared for user minimums. The mid-tier plan has a minimum of three users, and the most expensive plan has a minimum of 100 people. Key features of Dialpad Multi-level auto-attendants Team messaging Voicemail transcriptions Video meetings Analytics and reporting AI recaps Dialpad pricing For their Connect module, you can choose from three different Dialpad pricing plans : Standard: $15 per user per month for unlimited calling, AI-powered call and voicemail transcriptions, Dialpad SMS , and Google Workspace integrations Pro: $25 per user per month for the option to have additional numbers, Quality of Service reports, auto-replies, and CRM integrations, with a minimum of three users Enterprise: Call for a quote for unlimited locations and ring groups, SSO integrations, and live agent support, with a minimum of 100 users 7. Nextiva: Best for omnichannel communication Pros Omnichannel communication tools Digital service helpdesk tools Video meetings are available on the base plan Cons Limited SMS and MMS Toll-free numbers require an upgrade Call recording requires an add-on or plan upgrade Nextiva is cloud-based contact center software for managing customers across multiple digital touchpoints. The base plan gives you calling, texting, and video meetings. You can also connect up to three social media and online review channels. But the caveat is the price. The starter plan may look affordable. But if you look more closely, Nextiva locks some basic features behind upgrades and add-ons, forcing you to upgrade and pay more anyway. For example, you only get 100 texts per user per month on the base plan. Upgrading gets that number up to 500 texts. You also need to upgrade for toll-free numbers and call recording. Key features of Nextiva Video meetings Social media and review software integrations Live chat widgets AI call notes and summaries Nextiva pricing You can choose from three different Nextiva pricing plans : Core: $15 per user per month to access inbound and outbound voice calls, SMS/MMS up to 100 messages per user, voicemail transcriptions, and a simple IVR Engage: $25 per user per month to access call recording, a toll-free number and 2,000 toll-free minutes, 500 SMS/MMS per user, video meeting recording, and Microsoft Teams integration Scale: $75 per user per month for the inbound sales and service call center, priority and skills-based routing, supervisor dashboard, unlimited texting, up to 10,000 toll-free minutes, and automatic call distribution callback What you need to know about Verizon One Talk One Talk is a VoIP service you can add to Verizon’s traditional phone plans. You can use One Talk on your phone, tablet, desktop, or Verizon-approved desk phone. Besides calling and texting, it gives you features like auto receptionists and hunt groups. But it’s not clear which features you get on which plans or how much “extras” like phone menus might cost. One Talk is only available to Verizon business customers in the domestic US. So if you’re located in any other country, One Talk won’t be available to you. If you want to get a US number outside the US , you can use Verizon One Talk alternatives like Quo. Verizon One Talk pricing Sadly, the heading title is a bit anti-climactic. The truth is that there’s no public information on Verizon One Talk pricing . The only clear thing is that it starts at between $15 and $20 per number. When reaching out to Verizon, we were informed, “A One Talk representative will work with you to customize a package that meets your needs.” Why businesses turn to Verizon One Talk alternatives Verizon One Talk lacks clear pricing, reliability, and other key phone features businesses need. While you can make phone calls and send messages in the domestic US, you’ll be hard-pressed to do so at scale — and you won’t be able to do it at all without a preexisting Verizon phone plan. Here are a few more reasons One Talk customers switch to another provider: Call reliability issues Low call reliability is one of the most frequently cited issues for Verizon One Talk customers. Take a look at these reviews: “We switched 9 facilities from ATT to Verizon about a year ago. We run everything from restaurants to golf courses to fitness centers. We also run a very busy municipal building. We have been very disappointed. Overall, call quality is poor. Two of our facilities have broken calls constantly. We have tried EVERYTHING to solve the issues. The phones lose their 911 addressing info a lot, which renders them useless.” — VoIP Review “I am currently using one talk for my single business line, and it’s absolutely horrible, and I have not found a better option… The call quality is horrendous though, even with just my one line using on my personal cell.” — Reddit “…the service … is glitchy as heck. Calls are dropped repeatedly (always says “Reconnecting”), and notifications take forever to come through. Making calls out often says “you have limited connectivity” and therefore I … have to reach out on my SAME phone and call customers from my personal number…” — App Store Poor customer service If you run into trouble with your VoIP number, One Talk’s customer service team may not be much help. Poor customer service is a recurring issue, with hundreds of customers airing their frustrations about the not-so-user-friendly system as well as frequent dropped calls . Take a look: “So far, every single thing about my experience with this service has been horrible. All I needed was a second number for my business… Five hours on the phone with support and multiple more by myself troubleshooting…. Terrible, terrible, terrible. I can’t imagine a worse service.” — App Store “I dropped AT&T business lines to go with One Talk because they pitched it so well. However, it’s been a nightmare. Calls are dropped, when you download the app for some reason it [hijacks] our text from our personal number, and some texts don’t come through.” — Gartner “Each call to Verizon customer service could only contain one problem. Efforts to solve multiple problems in a single call (ticket) [that were] causing failures in the Verizon system, [required] multiple callbacks by me to clear the failed ticket before a new single-issue ticket could be initiated. The resolution of each problem required no less than 8 calls to Verizon customer service, involving a new person with each call [who had] no idea or interest other than reviewing the account in order to sell us additional services.” — VoIP Review Desk phones have to be purchased from Verizon One Talk’s desk phones are essentially business landlines. According to the latest available public information, desk phones have to be purchased directly from Verizon to be compatible with One Talk. You can’t use any preexisting hardware at all, making your upfront costs even higher. Call routing limitations Verizon’s simultaneous ring is a call routing feature that rings multiple devices at the same time when you receive an incoming call. In theory, this should help ensure that no call goes unanswered. However, it comes with limitations. You can only have up to 10 devices ringing at once per number, which may not be enough for larger teams that have multiple people handling calls. Even more limiting, Verizon caps active calls at just three per number — so even if multiple reps are available, only three conversations can happen at the same time. Lack of ways to save time on repetitive tasks One Talk offers little to help teams cut down on repetitive, manual work. For example, it doesn’t offer SMs templates to speed up sending repetitive messages. It also doesn’t let you schedule texts to go out in advance. Want to sync information between different tools so you’re not stuck manually entering the same information twice? The tool only connects with Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, or Salesforce. But there wasn’t enough information publicly available for us to confirm how many tools you can connect at the same time or what other integrations they have. Verizon One Talk does have an AI feature. Emphasis on “ an.” With One Talk, you get Verizon Business Assistant. This is an AI-powered texting tool that responds to customer questions automatically using a knowledge base you build. And it escalates to a live team member when it doesn’t know the answer. But that’s where One Talk’s AI stops. Compared to modern alternatives like Quo, One Talk lacks AI built for a team’s own workflow. For example, you don’t get call transcription or AI-generated call summaries. This can hold your team back compared to competitors that do save more time with productivity features. Quo: The best Verizon One Talk alternative Finding a great VoIP doesn’t have to feel like a task that takes weeks or months. With Quo, we’ve made it easy to start calling and texting fast. Our pricing is business-friendly and transparent. There are zero contracts, and we offer a free trial so you’re sure you like Quo before committing. Your team can automate routine tasks in your workflows and easily work together to respond to calls and texts. We offer affordable additional numbers and dozens of time-saving features so that as your team scales, Quo can grow alongside you. See for yourself why thousands of businesses use Quo by starting a free trial today . FAQs What is Verizon One Talk? Verizon One Talk is a mobile-first business phone solution. It lets you use one business number across multiple devices. This includes smartphones, tablets, computers, and supported desk phones. What are the best alternatives to Verizon One Talk for small businesses? The best alternative is Quo. With Quo, you get transparent pricing starting at $15 per user per month. Each user gets a local or toll-free number, and you have unlimited calling and texting in the US and Canada. Unlike One Talk, you don’t need an existing Verizon Wireless plan to sign up, and setup takes minutes rather than a conversation with a sales rep. Can you use Verizon One Talk outside the US? No, Verizon states One Talk is available to new or existing Verizon Business customers in the domestic US only. How long does it take to set up a Verizon One Talk alternative? Verizon One Talk alternatives like Quo let you sign up and start calling within 15 minutes to an hour. Just know that if you’re texting US customers, you have to complete carrier registration, which can take 2–7 days. If you’re porting a number to Quo , it can take 3–10 business days, depending on your carrier. These timeframes are common among VoIP providers and not specific to Quo. Is Verizon One Talk secure? Verizon claims to provide enterprise-grade security features. It also includes spam and fraud call filtering. But it doesn’t publish security certifications or compliance documentation for One Talk the way other providers do. How does Verizon One Talk work? One Talk lets a business share one phone number across multiple devices. It runs on top of an existing Verizon Business Wireless plan and is managed through the One Talk portal. This is where you can configure features like call routing, hunt groups, and auto attendants. Can I keep my existing phone number when switching from Verizon One Talk? Yes, in most cases. You can port an existing number when moving to a new provider, though the process and timeline vary depending on your new provider and number type. Can I get a toll-free number with Verizon One Talk? Toll-free numbers aren’t a standard, self-serve part of the core One Talk feature set. Verizon offers toll-free service, think numbers starting with 8XX, as a separate business product. So you’d need to check with a Verizon rep on how it integrates with One Talk specifically. Alternatives like Quo, by contrast, include a toll-free number with every user on the plan.

title: Some 4th of July doomerism: Is AGI an endgame for actuaries?
summary: Predictions by an investor who came to insurance sure AGI would delete the actuary, but left thinking actuaries are irreplaceable surgeons in the insurance org.
body_text: Some 4th of July doomerism: Is AGI an endgame for actuaries? Predictions by an investor who came to insurance sure AGI would delete the actuary, but left thinking actuaries are irreplaceable surgeons in the insurance org. AI for Actuaries @Tesora.ai and Vivek Jul 02, 2026 I am not an actuary. I am on the other side of the curve, an AI enthusiast who assumes almost every white-collar job is a wrapper around a model that does not quite exist yet but soon will. When I went looking for the industries that fall first, insurance initially sat at the top of my list. On paper, it seems like a very automatable business in the economy. A claim about risk, backed by data, sold to someone willing to stand behind it. That is the whole thing. Point a good enough model at the data and the humans start to look like latency. The more I looked, the more the setup confirmed the thesis. Insurance MGAs are people focused on specialist distribution – think Jiffy Lubes, car rentals, ATVs, funerals, anything you can hang a loss distribution on. The old end-to-end carrier long ago shattered into specialists: retail broker, wholesale broker, MGA, and paper that has drifted toward commodity, with reinsurers trading perils the way an FX desk trades currency. Every one of those layers, when you squint, is the same actuarial function wearing a different suit. Pricing is modeling. Reserving is modeling. Setting an appetite is modeling with a dial on it. Four copies of one job, each charging a toll, and the cost of that job is sliding toward zero. This was going to be easy. And the models did get good. Not demo-good. Good enough that the people inside stopped re-checking them on routine work, the way you stop re-checking a junior in year two. That is the threshold that matters, because it is the moment a company wires the model straight into its own data and lets it act. The exposure already lives in a warehouse. Soon the warehouse hands the whole thing to an insurance endpoint that reads it, runs the claims logic, and returns a bound price. The insurance company stops being a place you call and becomes an MCP you talk through. The broker-to-MGA-to-paper relay collapses into one endpoint. I had the blog post half-written. Then I met the actuary, and my thesis walked into a wall. The machine runs at full speed right up to one desk, and then it stops. Somebody has to explain the number to a regulator who did not enjoy their morning. Somebody has to still be there, in person, when the book develops badly and a plaintiff’s attorney wants to know who set the rate and what they were thinking. This is a profession that gets sued for being wrong slowly, and slow wrongness is exactly what a fluent machine is best at hiding. I had been treating the actuary’s signature as a ceremony. It is not a ceremony. It is more like a surgeon’s hand. Let me explain. The entire value of the signature is that a human with a career to lose looked at the thing and said yes. That was the analogy that reorganized my thinking. We have had AI reading scans better than radiologists for years, and the famous prediction that it would end the specialty simply did not happen, because someone still has to be accountable in the room when a life is on the table. The actuary is the surgeon of the balance sheet. The model can imagine the risk all day. It cannot be the one who is liable when the incision goes wrong, and you do not actually want it to be, because the entire value of the signature is that a human with a career to lose looked at the thing and said yes. With that, here is my predicted timeline of where we are going, as someone who once badly wanted the aggressive version to be true. In 2026, “Copilots” everywhere and trust nowhere. By 2027 someone runs a small, boring book where the model writes the rate and the actuary merely signs it, and that book runs at an expense ratio the rest of the company cannot match, the kind of number a CFO cannot un-see. By 2028 an AI-native MGA exposes its underwriting as an endpoint. By 2029 the bill comes due for whoever let an over-eager machine rubber-stamp its way through a book, because slow wrongness only starts to show up after two years. The winners are not the firms that removed the actuary. They are the firms that aimed all that automation at everything except the signature, and kept a surgeon on call. I stopped believing accountability is a task you can hand to something with nothing to lose. A model cannot be sued, cannot be sanctioned, and cannot lose a license it never held, and those are the exact levers that make a human signature mean anything. So the actuary does not disappear. The actuary gets a smaller team, a wider blast radius on every decision, and a machine that has finally worked out why there was a human standing there in the first place. Maybe one day the judgment itself loads into the model like a skill and the room gets smaller still. Until then, the winning move is not to replace the surgeon. It is to hand them a better prepared operating room, and let them continue handling the incisions. title: Con Edison Asks Customers In Areas of Queens to Conserve Energy
body_text: Con Edison is asking some customers in southeastern Queens to conserve energy while crews repair equipment. Con Edison has reduced voltage by 8 percent to the area while repairs are completed. The area is bounded by Grand Central Parkway on the north, Jamaica Bay on south, the Nassau County line on the east, and Queens Boulevard and the Van Wyck Expressway on the west. It includes parts, or all, of these neighborhoods: Bellaire, Bellerose, Cambria Heights, Floral Park, Glen Oaks, Hollis, Holliswood, Jamaica, Jamaica Hills, Laurelton, Queens Village, Springfield Gardens, St. Albans and South Jamaica. The area has 163,000 customers. The equipment problems in these neighborhoods have no effect on the rest of the Con Edison system. Con Edison has asked customers in these areas not to use energy-intensive appliances such as washers, dryers, and microwaves until crews complete repairs. The company also asks customers to limit unnecessary use of air conditioning. If you have two air conditioners, use only one and set it to the highest comfortable temperature. The company also asks that drivers refrain from charging their electric vehicles, except when necessary, until repairs are made. Customers can report outages and check service restoration status at www.conEd.com/reportoutage , or with our mobile app for iOS or Android devices, or by calling 1-800-75-CONED ( 1-800-752-6633 ). When calling, customers should report whether their neighbors also have lost power. Customers can follow Con Edison on X , Instagram or like us on Facebook for general outage updates, safety tips and storm preparation information. The company is in communication with New York City Emergency Management.

title: Wabash Inks Partnership with Truck Source Inc. to Grow Western U.S. Dealer Footprint
summary: Expanded dealer network gives western U.S. fleets faster access to equipment, parts and service that keep operations moving
body_text: Expanded dealer network gives western fleets faster access to equipment, parts and service that keep operations moving Wabash (NYSE: WNC), a leader in end-to-end supply chain solutions for the transportation, logistics and infrastructure markets, today announced a new partnership with Truck Source Inc., a full-service trailer dealership headquartered in Portland, Oregon. The partnership strengthens Wabash's ability to serve fleets operating throughout the growing Interstate- 5 corridor and greater Phoenix market. This partnership expands customer access to trailers, parts and service, making it easier for local and national fleets to get the equipment and support they need across the Western U.S. It also reflects Wabash’s commitment to partnering with dealers known for responsive service, technical expertise and scalable support that help keep customers operating with confidence. With full-service locations in Portland, Oregon, and Phoenix, Arizona, Truck Source will offer Wabash's complete lineup of dry van trailers, platform trailers and truck bodies, along with warranty support, maintenance and replacement parts. Since its founding in 2002, Truck Source has been a family-owned and operated commercial truck and trailer dealership with more than two decades of experience serving transportation customers. The company provides trailer and truck sales, maintenance, repairs, parts and fleet support, building long-term relationships through responsive service, personalized customer care and dependable support that helps fleets maximize equipment uptime. "Wabash is committed to expanding our dealer network with partners who share our focus on helping customers operate with confidence," said Drew Schwartzhoff, chief commercial officer at Wabash. "Truck Source has built a strong reputation for responsive service, technical expertise and customer relationships throughout the Pacific Northwest and Arizona. Together, we’ll make it easier for fleets to access the equipment, parts and support they need to maximize uptime and keep business moving." The addition of Truck Source expands Wabash's ability to support fleets operating in key freight markets where dependable equipment, responsive service and timely parts availability help keep freight moving and reduce costly downtime. Portland serves as a strategic hub along the I-5 corridor connecting the West Coast to Canada, while Phoenix continues to experience significant growth as a transportation and logistics center. "For more than 20 years, Truck Source has built our business on keeping fleets moving," said Alex Bessarab, president of Truck Source. "Partnering with Wabash lets us pair best-in-class trailer products with the service, parts and warranty support our customers rely on to keep equipment on the road. We are excited about what this partnership means for carriers throughout Oregon and Arizona and excited to grow alongside Wabash as we help keep our customers on the road." The Wabash Truck Source partnership expands customer access to equipment, parts and service while strengthening regional support capabilities. It reflects Wabash’s continued investment in a connected dealer network that helps simplify fleet operations, maximize equipment uptime and deliver long-term value to customers.

title: Net Lease Retail is at an Inflection Point
summary: As retail investors and operators convene in Las Vegas for ICSC, the conversation around net lease retail feels both familiar and different. Familiar, because the net lease retail market continues to demonstrate resilience and stability. Different, because the drivers shaping today’s retail real estate decisions are evolving—creating new opportunities for operators and investors alike.
body_text: Subscribe to the Blog Thought Leadership | May 11, 2026 Net Lease Retail is at an Inflection Point Key trends ahead of ICSC Las Vegas By: Michael Fitzgerald As retail investors and operators convene in Las Vegas for ICSC, the conversation around net lease retail feels both familiar and different. Familiar, because the net lease retail market continues to demonstrate resilience and stability. Different, because the drivers shaping today’s retail real estate decisions are evolving—creating new opportunities for operators and investors alike. From rising sale-leaseback activity tied to M&A, to more intentional approaches around store size and format, today’s net lease retail market is being shaped by a combination of strategic growth decisions, changing consumer behavior and a more balanced transactional environment. These are several of the key trends taking center stage ahead of the conference. Sale-leasebacks Follow Strategic M&A Activity One of the most consistent drivers of sale-leaseback volume in retail today is merger and acquisition activity. Whether it involves private equity-backed platforms consolidating regional brands or strategic buyers acquiring complementary concepts, transactions often prompt companies to reassess their balance sheets—and real estate frequently emerges as one of the most efficient sources of capital. In many cases, companies come out of acquisitions with real estate portfolios that were not central to the strategic rationale of the deal. Sale-leasebacks allow operators to unlock that capital, streamline their asset base and redeploy proceeds into higher-return priorities such as new stores, technology investments or debt reduction. What stands out in the current environment is that this activity is not limited to highly leveraged situations. Healthy, growing retailers are increasingly using sale-leasebacks proactively as part of longer-term capital planning, particularly when M&A introduces scale or accelerates geographic expansion. Sale-leasebacks continue to provide a compelling alternative to traditional financing for businesses seeking flexibility and predictability. The Evolution Toward Smaller, More Flexible Footprints Another defining trend across retail is the ongoing evolution of physical store footprints. While large-format locations remain relevant in certain categories, many retailers are gravitating toward smaller, more efficient concepts that align with omnichannel strategies and localized demand. These stores are often designed to serve multiple functions—acting as showrooms, service hubs, fulfillment points or a combination of the three. Flexibility has become increasingly important, both in store design and in location strategy, as retailers respond to shifting consumer behavior. From a net lease perspective, this evolution places greater emphasis on unit-level fundamentals. Smaller footprints can generate compelling cash-on-cash returns, but success depends heavily on the alignment between location, concept and the operating model. The underwriting process for net lease retail investors is therefore increasingly focused on how these formats perform across markets, how scalable they are and how they fit into a retailer’s broader growth strategy. Stabilized Cap Rates Bring Predictability Back to the Market After a period of volatility driven by rapid interest-rate movements, cap rates across the net lease retail space have begun to stabilize. While pricing discipline remains essential, the return of predictability has had a meaningful impact on transaction activity. Clearer valuation benchmarks make it easier for buyers and sellers to transact. Investors can underwrite opportunities with greater confidence, tenants can assess capital alternatives more thoughtfully and deals are less likely to stall amid uncertainty around pricing expectations. That said, credit quality, location fundamentals, lease structure and real estate criticality remain core considerations. However, in a more balanced environment, high-quality assets supported by strong operators are finding liquidity, and capital is moving more efficiently. Looking Ahead As ICSC Las Vegas approaches, there is optimism across the net lease retail landscape. While uncertainty remains part of the broader economic backdrop, the conversations in Las Vegas are expected to reflect an industry that has evolved through recent cycles and continues to find opportunity through change. For net lease retail, the current environment represents less of a reset and more of a recalibration—one that rewards sound fundamentals, flexibility and a long-term investment approach. Michael Fitzgerald Managing Director Head of U.S. Retail Investments View bio Related Topics: Thought Leadership Retail Sale-leaseback M&A You May Also Like: WPC in the News Net Lease Retail Demand Follows Where Retailers Are Growing The US net lease market is experiencing a resurgence. Valuations reset throughout 2025, meaning the bid-ask spread narrowed. And in spite of economic headwinds, net lease volumes increased by 24% year-over-year for the fiscal year ending in Q3 2025, according to CBRE. For Michael Fitzgerald, managing director and head of US retail at W. P. Carey, finding the right retail investment opportunity starts with understanding some tell-tale signals. “The US net lease retail environment is driven primarily by the general health of retailers,” says Fitzgerald. “Are there a large number of retail operators that are opening new locations or investing in existing locations in a way where they need access to capital?” When the answer to that question is yes, deal flow often follows, and Fitzgerald points to specific categories where he sees the strongest deal flow and investor interest right now. Non-discretionary Categories Draw Investor Interest Fitzgerald notes that retailers that sell non-discretionary products or services are among the most interesting for investors, but tend to carry lower cap rates. “We also think about the macro trends, such as fitness,” says Fitzgerald. “It used to be something that a small percentage of the population would pay for; now it’s become a non-discretionary spend for a lot of families because general health and fitness have become a priority.” He notes that convenience stores, car washes and automotive services are among the other segments he sees generating strong deal flow, with car washes having regained interest and automotive services drawing attention across the board. Full Loan-to-Value Appeal Drives Demand For business operators or CFOs seeking efficient forms of capital, Fitzgerald explains that the net lease structure is hard to beat. “They can redeploy that capital back into their businesses at a higher return because they’re getting more loan-to-value than a mortgage,” says Fitzgerald. “That’s why we see sale-leasebacks continuing to be one of the top choices for businesses that have an ongoing need for capital.” When evaluating a net lease retail asset, Fitzgerald explains that the analysis centers on whether a location can generate enough cash flow to cover rent easily across a commitment that can run for 20 years or more. He also notes that new stores can complicate that picture since there is no operating history to draw from, which is why assets with longer track records tend to be the easiest to understand and underwrite. Net Lease Retail Holds Up Across Good Economies and Bad Despite continued headlines about retailer store closures, Fitzgerald notes that the net lease retail market is more durable than the news cycle suggests. He explains that the net lease market has proved resilient across good and bad economies, with the most difficult periods coming not from downturns but from rapid interest rate swings in either direction. “I’m optimistic about the net lease retail market. Even in times of relative instability, we continue to see consistent deal flow, as companies leverage sale-leaseback transactions to monetize real estate and fund growth,” says Fitzgerald. Thought Leadership ICSC Las Vegas Preview ICSC Las Vegas, one of the largest commercial real estate gatherings, will again convene the industry’s leading professionals and retailers next week. Over 30,000 attendees will gather for networking, deal-making and insights into how the retail real estate industry will fare amid a volatile and uncertain economic environment. Tariffs, shifts in consumer sentiment and sale-leaseback opportunities will be among the biggest topics discussed at the conference. Outlined below is an overview of each. Tariffs add pressure and uncertainty for retailers Uncertainty surrounding tariffs is expected to have a substantial impact on the retail real estate industry. The National Retail Federation announced it expects the growth of U.S. retail sales to slow down this year due to consumer anxiety and inflation, with an outsized impact on smaller retailers and certain industries including textiles and electronics. While the long-term impact of tariff policies is unclear, retailers ultimately will have to determine how much of the additional costs they can absorb versus passing on to consumers. These decisions could have significant impacts on retailers’ balance sheets and ability to remain operational, affecting overall investment in the sector. Consumer sentiment shifts will impact investor demand Shifting consumer preferences continue to present both opportunities and challenges for retailers. Uncertainty surrounding the future of the economy has made consumers more budget conscious and focused on necessities. According to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, essential goods account for 65% of consumer spending. As a result, retailers will likely continue to show interest in grocery-anchored shopping centers, which continue to remain among the best-performing retail property types. E-commerce also continues to redefine retail. As more consumers shift their spending online, retailers like Macy’s are consolidating locations and shrinking their footprints. For investors seeking stability, this means targeting markets with strong population and job growth—where retail assets are most likely to perform well over the long term. Sale-leasebacks remain a viable financing option Despite economic uncertainty, the retail sale-leaseback market continues to grow—thanks to its clear advantages over traditional debt. By unlocking the full market value of their real estate, retailers can reinvest proceeds into their core business and drive stronger returns. Sale-leasebacks also provide long-term capital with no refinancing risk and typically without the restrictive debt covenants or balloon payments that come with conventional financing. In today’s climate, where liquidity and balance sheet flexibility are paramount, that kind of stability is more valuable than ever. Thought Leadership Countdown to ICSC Las Vegas ICSC Las Vegas, one of the largest tradeshows for the retail industry, is on the horizon with an expected 30,000 attendees eager to network and reconnect face-to-face with industry leaders and peers. After a somewhat sluggish 2023, attendees will be looking to the conference to shed some light on the retail landscape and offer insights on new trends and opportunities within the sector. Consumer spending, retail vacancies and sale-leaseback activity will be among the most pressing topics discussed at the show. Here's an overview of each: Consumer spending remains steady Despite inflationary concerns, consumer spending has remained steady over the past year, as core retail sales, excluding gasoline, food service and auto vehicle purchases, increased by 3.3% at the end of 2023. As a result, demand for retail space has remained strong and the market is starting to see in uptick in new developer-built retail locations coming online. W. P. Carey has completed several deals that align with this trend – for example, the acquisition of 22 recently built and to-be-completed car wash facilities across the U.S., leased to Tidal Wave Auto Spa, a prominent car wash operator. With interest rates projected to decrease in late 2024, the market will likely continue to see a ramp up in new development over the coming months. Retail vacancies at record lows Strong demand for retail space has resulted in record-low vacancy rates, with total retail vacancy reaching 4.2% at the end of 2023. Low vacancy rates are a positive sign for investors like W. P. Carey as it provides greater confidence in long-term leases and the ability to re-lease vacant buildings if the need arises. However, it also means more competition for less space which is pushing retail rents significantly higher. This makes it more expensive for retailers looking to expand and acquire new space, which in turn increases operational costs. Sale-leaseback activity picks up With rents rising significantly, retailers – particularly those looking to grow their real estate footprints – will be seeking new ways to access capital. This will likely contribute to greater demand for sale-leasebacks, where a retailer sells its real estate to an investor (like W. P. Carey) for cash and simultaneously enters into a long-term lease. This is a valuable business decision for most retail companies because owning real estate can serve as a drag on their balance sheet. By unlocking the value of their real estate through a sale-leaseback, retailers can reinvest proceeds into their core competencies, leading to better overall returns and long-term growth.
